summary.text: Joe Neguse is the Democratic incumbent for Colorado's 2nd District, first elected in 2018. A University of Colorado graduate, he co-founded the civic group New Era Colorado, served on the University of Colorado Board of Regents, and led Colorado's consumer-protection agency before entering Congress. In the House he serves on the Natural Resources, Judiciary and Rules committees and, since March 2024, as Assistant Democratic Leader.

paragraphs.text: Neguse was born May 13, 1984, in Bakersfield, California; his parents immigrated from Eritrea, and the family moved to Colorado when he was six.
He earned a B.S. in political science and economics, graduating summa cum laude, from the University of Colorado Boulder and a J.D. from the University of Colorado School of Law.
He co-founded New Era Colorado, a youth civic-engagement organization.
In 2008 he was elected to the University of Colorado Board of Regents for the 2nd Congressional District and served a six-year term.
Neguse served in Gov. John Hickenlooper's cabinet as executive director of the Colorado Department of Regulatory Agencies from 2015 to 2017.
He was elected to the U.S. House in 2018 and, according to his official biography, is Colorado's first Black member of Congress.
He serves on the Natural Resources, Judiciary and Rules committees and is ranking member of the Federal Lands subcommittee, per his official biography.
In March 2024 he was elected House Assistant Minority Leader (Assistant Democratic Leader).
According to his office, Neguse was named among the most effective lawmakers by the Center for Effective Lawmaking and has authored laws on public lands, rural schools and small business.
He lives in Lafayette, Colorado, with his wife, Andrea, and their two children, according to his official biography.
